papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Towards Imperceptible and Robust Adversarial Example Attacks against Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Machine learning systems based on deep neural networks, being able to produce state-of-the-art results on various perception tasks, have gained mainstream adoption in many applications. However, they are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial example attack, which generates malicious output by adding slight perturbations to the input. Previous adversarial example crafting methods, however, use simple metrics to evaluate the distances between the original examples and the adversarial ones, which could be easily detected by human eyes. In addition, these attacks are often not robust due to the inevitable noises and deviation in the physical world. In this work, we present a new adversarial example attack crafting method, which takes the human perceptual system into consideration and maximizes the noise tolerance of the crafted adversarial example. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

summary: The retrieved literature addresses the critical vulnerabilities of AI systems, particularly in recommendation and computer vision domains, against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. Proposed frameworks emphasize innovative defense mechanisms such as robust loss functions, GAN-based detection, and frequency domain manipulation, yet they often lack scalability and comprehensive evaluation across diverse datasets. Notably, there is a significant research gap in developing adaptable and efficient strategies to enhance AI resilience against evolving adversarial threats, particularly in real-world applications.
scholarly_positioning: While existing literature has made strides in addressing the vulnerabilities of AI systems to data poisoning and adversarial attacks, the proposed defense mechanisms often suffer from limitations in scalability and applicability across diverse real-world scenarios. For instance, frameworks focusing on specific domains, such as recommendation systems, fail to generalize to other AI applications, leaving a gap in adaptable defense strategies. Furthermore, the lack of comprehensive empirical evaluations across varied datasets and attack types underscores the insufficiency of current approaches. This research aims to bridge these gaps by developing a robust and scalable defense framework that not only enhances resilience against evolving adversarial threats but also maintains model performance across multiple AI domains.
research_scope: This study will focus on developing a robust and scalable defense framework for image classification models in the domain of computer vision, specifically targeting the vulnerabilities posed by data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The framework will incorporate techniques such as robust loss functions, anomaly detection, and frequency domain manipulation, with an evaluation period spanning six months to assess its effectiveness across multiple datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. A control group will consist of baseline models without the proposed defenses to facilitate comparative analysis. Primary outcomes will include model accuracy and resilience against adversarial attacks, while secondary outcomes will assess computational efficiency and scalability of the defense mechanisms in real-world applications.
concept_definition:
{
  "robust AI systems": "AI systems designed to maintain performance and accuracy despite adversarial attacks or data poisoning.",
  "data poisoning": "A type of attack where malicious data is introduced into the training dataset to manipulate the model's behavior.",
  "adversarial attacks": "Techniques that involve altering input data to deceive AI models into making incorrect predictions.",
  "defense framework": "A structured approach incorporating various techniques to protect AI models from vulnerabilities.",
  "robust loss functions": "Loss functions designed to minimize the impact of outliers and adversarial examples during model training.",
  "anomaly detection": "Techniques used to identify and respond to unusual patterns in data that may indicate a security threat.",
  "frequency domain manipulation": "Techniques that modify the frequency components of input data to enhance model robustness against attacks.",
  "image classification models": "AI models specifically trained to categorize images into predefined classes.",
  "CIFAR-10": "A dataset commonly used for training machine learning models, consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images in 10 classes.",
  "ImageNet": "A large visual database designed for use in visual object recognition software research, containing millions of labeled images.",
  "baseline models": "Standard models used for comparison that do not incorporate the proposed defense mechanisms.",
  "model accuracy": "The percentage of correct predictions made by the model compared to the total number of predictions.",
  "resilience against adversarial attacks": "The ability of a model to maintain performance when subjected to adversarial inputs.",
  "computational efficiency": "The measure of the resources required (time, memory) for the model to operate effectively.",
  "scalability": "The capability of the defense mechanisms to maintain performance when applied to larger datasets or more complex scenarios.",
  "real-world applications": "Practical implementations of AI models in various domains outside of controlled experimental settings.",
  "trust calibration": "The alignment between a user's perceived trust in a model and the model's actual performance.",
  "perceived transparency": "The degree to which users feel they understand how a model makes its decisions."

gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of various defense mechanisms against data poisoning and adversarial attacks in AI systems, particularly in recommendation and computer vision contexts; however, they treat the scalability and adaptability of these defenses across diverse applications as secondary, leaving unclear whether the proposed methods can maintain performance in real-world scenarios. This matters practically because the evolving nature of adversarial threats necessitates robust defenses that can generalize across different AI domains; therefore, this study investigates the development of a scalable defense framework that enhances resilience against these threats while ensuring model performance in image classification tasks.
question: How does the implementation of a robust and scalable defense framework, incorporating techniques such as robust loss functions and anomaly detection, affect the resilience and accuracy of image classification models against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to baseline models without these defenses?
theoretical_mechanism: The independent variable is the implementation of a robust and scalable defense framework, which includes robust loss functions and anomaly detection techniques. The mediator is the model's resilience against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, which is influenced by the defense mechanisms enhancing the model's ability to detect and mitigate malicious inputs. The dependent variable is the accuracy of image classification models, which is expected to improve as a result of the enhanced resilience. The theoretical framework is based on adversarial machine learning, where the causal chain posits that improved defense mechanisms lead to better detection and mitigation of attacks, thus maintaining model performance. System-level outcomes include reduced unsafe response rates and improved refusal accuracy, while user-level outcomes involve increased trust and satisfaction, mediated by perceived transparency in the model's decision-making process. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of the defense mechanisms across diverse datasets and the extent to which perceived transparency influences user trust in model outputs.
hypothesis: The implementation of a robust and scalable defense framework, incorporating robust loss functions and anomaly detection, will significantly improve the resilience of image classification models against data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to baseline models without these defenses, leading to higher model accuracy.

phd_contribution_design: This research proposes a novel defense framework that integrates robust loss functions and anomaly detection to enhance the resilience of image classification models against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The mechanism-level claim posits that these techniques work synergistically to improve model performance by effectively detecting and mitigating malicious inputs. Existing literature fails to comprehensively address the scalability and adaptability of defense mechanisms across diverse AI applications, particularly in real-world scenarios. The falsifiable scientific claim is that the implementation of the proposed framework will lead to a statistically significant improvement in model accuracy compared to baseline models without these defenses. The strongest baseline for comparison will be standard image classification models trained without any defense mechanisms. Evidence supporting the claim will be derived from rigorous empirical evaluations showing improved accuracy and reduced adversarial attack success rates. A negative or null result would suggest that the proposed defense mechanisms do not significantly enhance model resilience, challenging the theoretical framework and necessitating a reevaluation of the interaction between these techniques.

Lastly, the absence of ablation studies to isolate the contributions of each component of the defense framework is a critical oversight; the proposal must outline a strategy for conducting these studies to substantiate the claims made.

proposal: This research proposes the development of a novel, robust, and scalable defense framework specifically designed for image classification models in computer vision, addressing critical vulnerabilities to data poisoning and adversarial attacks. Unlike existing frameworks that often focus narrowly on specific domains or lack empirical validation across diverse datasets, this study integrates robust loss functions, anomaly detection, and frequency domain manipulation into a cohesive framework, providing a multi-faceted approach to enhance model resilience. The literature reveals significant gaps, particularly in the scalability and adaptability of defense mechanisms, as prior work has inadequately evaluated their effectiveness in real-world scenarios, often overlooking the interplay between model performance and defense complexity. This study aims to fill these gaps by establishing a clear theoretical mechanism: the proposed framework is expected to improve resilience (mediator) against adversarial threats, which in turn enhances model accuracy (dependent variable). The methodology includes a rigorous comparative analysis against baseline models without defenses, utilizing datasets such as CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, with clearly defined metrics for model accuracy and adversarial attack success rates. To ensure robust validation, the study will incorporate ablation studies to isolate the contributions of each defense component, control for confounding variables through standardized conditions, and employ statistical methods to assess the significance of results. This research not only advances theoretical understanding of defense mechanisms in AI but also provides actionable insights for practical deployment across various AI applications, thus addressing the pressing need for adaptable defenses in the face of evolving adversarial threats. By directly responding to the pre-proposal reviewer objections, this proposal articulates a clear path to empirical validation, situates the work within broader research debates, and delineates the novel contributions to the field of adversarial machine learning.
draft_proposal: This research proposes the development of a robust and scalable defense framework for image classification models in the domain of computer vision, specifically targeting vulnerabilities to data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The core concepts include robust AI systems, data poisoning, adversarial attacks, and defense frameworks, with a focus on techniques such as robust loss functions, anomaly detection, and frequency domain manipulation. The study will utilize labeled datasets like CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, requiring GPU resources for model training and evaluation. Scholarly positioning highlights the limitations of existing frameworks in scalability and adaptability across diverse applications, addressing a significant empirical gap in the literature regarding comprehensive evaluations of defense mechanisms. The research question investigates how the proposed defense framework affects model resilience and accuracy compared to baseline models without defenses. The theoretical mechanism posits that the implementation of the defense framework enhances resilience (mediator) leading to improved accuracy (dependent variable), with system-level outcomes including reduced unsafe response rates and user-level outcomes involving increased trust through perceived transparency. The falsifiable hypothesis states that the proposed framework will significantly improve model accuracy and resilience against attacks compared to baseline models. Construct operationalization involves measuring the robust defense framework through implementation metrics, resilience via adversarial attack success rates, and model accuracy through classification accuracy percentages. The methodology includes comparative analysis against baseline models, ensuring consistent dataset characteristics and architectures. The PhD contribution design emphasizes a comprehensive theoretical framework integrating robust loss functions and anomaly detection, addressing the scalability and adaptability of defense mechanisms. To counter reviewer concerns, the proposal includes a detailed empirical validation plan, specifies baseline models, and outlines strategies for conducting ablation studies to isolate contributions. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in understanding defense mechanisms, technical innovations in framework design, empirical insights from diverse evaluations, and practical deployment guidelines for real-world applications. Novelty is established through the unique integration of frequency domain manipulation with established techniques, while acknowledging limitations such as potential confounding variables and the need for continuous updates to the defense framework.
